title: Email & Lifecycle Automation
excerpt: Enterprise marketing automation: email and WhatsApp lifecycle flows, AI assistants and CRM integration. Find out more.
rm_desc: Enterprise marketing automation: email and WhatsApp lifecycle flows, AI assistants and CRM integration. Find out more.
content: Enterprise marketing automation is supposed to make leads convert while they are warm and customers come back without being chased manually, not turn every touchpoint into a robotic drip. Leads that wait, lapse. We automate the conversations and journeys around your marketing carefully, because over-automation is its own failure mode: premium buyers can tell when nobody’s home, and consent rules (PDPA here, and platform policies on WhatsApp) bound what good automation is allowed to do. The craft is knowing where the human takes over: email flows, WhatsApp and messaging automation, AI assistants, all wired into your CRM.
• Lifecycle email flows: nurture, cart recovery, re-engagement, repeat purchase
• WhatsApp and messaging automation for lead gen, enquiries and campaigns
• Conversational AI assistants across your site and messaging platforms
• AI-driven lead qualification and routing to the right sales team
• CRM and data integration so marketing sees what actually closed
Enterprise marketing automation, built for this region

A large share of Southeast Asian buying conversations happen in WhatsApp and chat, not email alone. Automation that ignores messaging automates the wrong channel, ours treats email and messaging as one lifecycle.
This is the conversion layer of our modular services: it makes the demand that paid media and social create actually land as revenue, with analytics proving it.

Most accounts we inherit are running three or four disconnected tools: an email platform that does not talk to the CRM, a WhatsApp inbox managed by hand, and a lead-scoring spreadsheet someone updates when they remember. Consolidating those into one enterprise marketing automation stack is not about buying a bigger tool, it is about making sure a lead’s behaviour in one channel actually changes what happens in the next one. A site visitor who abandons a cart should trigger a different WhatsApp message than one who is never visited at all; that only works if the systems share data in real time.

Automation makes it easy to message people more than they have agreed to. Singapore’s PDPA and WhatsApp’s own business messaging policy both set real limits on frequency and consent, and we build automation flows inside those limits rather than testing how far we can push before someone complains. An enterprise marketing automation programme that generates opt-outs faster than leads is not a success story, however good the open rates look in the monthly report.

The report that matters tracks revenue attributable to automated flows against the manual baseline they replaced, not open rates and click rates in isolation. A welcome sequence with a 60% open rate that converts nobody is not working, whatever the platform dashboard says about engagement. We report flow-level revenue and conversion rate monthly, alongside the operational metric that actually predicts both: list health, since a shrinking, disengaged list degrades every flow built on top of it regardless of how well each individual message is written.
Tools we build enterprise marketing automation on

We work inside whatever CRM and marketing platform a client already runs rather than forcing a migration for its own sake, since the cost of ripping out an embedded system rarely pays for itself in the improvement a newer tool offers. The exception is when the existing stack cannot do the job, no API access, no way to trigger messaging from behavioural data, in which case we will say so plainly and scope a migration as its own project with its own timeline, rather than quietly inflating the automation budget to cover a platform problem nobody actually asked us to go and solve in the first place.
